requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page served inside the live-animals journey at /<role path>/add-address that saves into the address book without the trader leaving the animals service.
requirements.why: Where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the single-app prototype cannot express, so the INS frontend stays the address book's only writer, reached through the journey handshake; the animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' links out to the INS frontend's /address-book/add (repo-frontend-p9-133, trace-e2e-p9-013), whose page sits in the INS layout (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1); the journey's own create page was retired and answers 404 (trace-e2e-p9-080).

requirements.statement: Every party picker (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination) and the consignment contact page has an 'Add a new address' link to the INS address book's /address-book/add, carrying journey-type 'gbn-ag', the notification reference, the role's fulfilment id (its obligation id) and a fresh handshake token, which the INS add page keeps as hidden fields and sends back unchanged; a role with no fulfilment mapping, or the frontend in stub mode, shows no add link.
requirements.why: The handshake is how the INS address book knows which notification and role to return the new address to; it stays because the INS frontend remains the address book's only writer (c-106). DR1 asked for a route to add an address from every address-selection page (inc-053), and it now exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today in ins-handshake.js (repo-frontend-p9-134, repo-frontend-p9-136): the pickers and the contact page link out with the four parameters (trace-e2e-p8-091, trace-e2e-p9-013), and the return is seen end to end (trace-e2e-p9-014, trace-e2e-p9-015, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1).

requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role ('Unknown fulfilment' otherwise) and its handshake token matches the single-use token remembered in a cookie for that role ('Invalid handshake' otherwise, including a missing token), and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today in address-return/controller.js (repo-frontend-p9-140, repo-frontend-p9-142, repo-frontend-p9-144).

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.', and an address book that cannot be reached, or a save that fails, shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-145, repo-frontend-p9-146, repo-frontend-p9-150, repo-frontend-p9-151).

requirements.statement: A trader with no INS session who follows 'Add a new address' signs in through Defra ID first and then lands on the INS add page with the handshake intact.
requirements.why: The INS frontend owns its own session and stays the address book's only writer (c-106); crossing to it must not lose which notification and role the address is for.
requirements.deltaNote: Seen today end to end (trace-e2e-p9-052).

requirements.statement: The manual-entry Country select on the add-address page stays a plain select (not the accessible autocomplete) and offers the countries reference-data serves from MDM (its unfiltered country list), never a list typed or edited in code; where that content differs from Design Release 2.1's 42 entries (such as the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies), the difference is MDM's content to change, and the page's tests take country names and counts from the captured reference-data fixture, not a hand-typed list.

requirements.statement: Every add-address page that searches (the consignee, importer and place of destination pages reached from the journey, and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step) starts with a UK address search: a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search icon button whose accessible name is 'Search', which submits the search to the server so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds UK addresses by search rather than typing them in; every search is a form with a button that submits it, so the page works without JavaScript (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today: the INS add page is typed in by hand (trace-e2e-p9-058).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.statement: Submitting the address search lists matching UK addresses under 'Address search results', each a choice showing the organisation name and the full one-line address; Northern Ireland addresses are not offered.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search results, in the version that works without JavaScript (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); results that appear as the trader types are a separate, design-blocked requirement.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.statement: The address search announces its result count to screen readers through a polite live region, such as '1 result available'.
requirements.why: Screen reader users must hear that results have appeared as they type; a custom announcement is JavaScript-only behaviour, so it waits on design as well as the lookup (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; this is one waiting-on-design increment. It is also blocked until the INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in), and the address search area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result fills name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all still editable; email address and phone number stay empty for the trader to complete; any earlier error messages stay until the next submit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pick behaviour, in the version that works without JavaScript: the pick is submitted and the page comes back filled. Hiding the search box on a pick is part of the design-blocked search-only layout (req-653).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.statement: Picking a search result never drops part of the address the lookup returned: a locality (such as Kirkby in 'Depot road, Kirkby, Liverpool') is kept in the filled form.
requirements.why: The prototype loses the locality because its form has no field for it; a saved address missing part of itself is a real data constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; this is one waiting-on-design increment. requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; this is one waiting-on-design increment. requirements.statement: The add-address page asks 'What else should this address be used for?' as a checkbox fieldset.

requirements.statement: The uses question's hint reads 'This address is being added as a <Role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', naming the role's own label (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer or Place of destination) and using 'an' before Importer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; it tells the trader the role they came from is already implied.

requirements.statement: The uses checkboxes offer only the other roles on the same side, each labelled with the role name alone: place of origin offers 'Consignor'; consignor offers 'Place of origin'; consignee offers 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'; importer offers 'Consignee' and 'Place of destination'; place of destination offers 'Consignee' and 'Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never lets an origin-side address be marked for a destination-side role, or the other way round.

requirements.statement: No uses checkbox is preselected, ticking none raises no error, a value not offered for the role is discarded, and the ticked uses are kept when the page is shown again with errors.
requirements.why: The role the trader came from is implied; the extra uses are optional.

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved in the address book carrying the role it was added for plus every use ticked, so the address book record holds its roles, in a field shape the address book service designs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the address with its types, and ruling 2026-10-09 keeps address uses and roles because a kept question must persist and DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers; today's record has no field to hold them, so the address book's persistence changes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an address book record holds id, name, address fields, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, deleted and timestamps, with no role or type (trace-e2e-p8-012).

requirements.statement: A failed submit of the add-address page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing every error in field order (seven on a blank manual page), each repeated inline with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix and the field in its GOV.UK error style, and keeps everything the trader entered.

requirements.statement: The add-address page keeps the address book's length and format checks beyond the required-field checks: name and address lines 255 characters or fewer, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20, email 254 and in a valid format, each with today's message (such as 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer' and 'Enter an email address in the correct format').
requirements.why: The address book stores and validates these limits; a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides its required-only checks.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already carry these checks and messages (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-frontend-p9-115, repo-frontend-p9-120; trace-e2e-p8-049, trace-e2e-p8-050).

requirements.statement: A refused add-address submit answers HTTP 400 and prefixes the browser title with 'Error: '.

requirements.statement: The add-address page's fields carry browser autocomplete hints: organization for the name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 for town or city, postal-code, email and tel.

requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page sets autocomplete only on the email field (trace-e2e-p9-065); the journey's edit page already sets them all (repo-frontend-p9-103-m1).

requirements.statement: 'Save and select' saves the new address to the address book, puts a copy of it on the notification for the role it was added for, and returns the trader to the Consignment addresses page, where the role shows the address with a 'Change' link.

requirements.statement: After either save, the page the trader lands on shows a GOV.UK notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which stays on screen until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1, like DR1, confirms the address went into the address book; a message that leaves on a timer fails WCAG 2.2.1 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows only the 'Selected address: <name>' inset, no banner (trace-e2e-p9-072).

requirements.statement: The add-address page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link to the notification's hub, which saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a secondary 'Cancel and return to address page' button returns the trader to the role's picker, saving nothing (trace-e2e-p9-075, trace-e2e-p9-076, repo-tests-p5-031).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every role picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS save creates the record in the organisation's book and the picker count rises (trace-e2e-p8-011, trace-e2e-p9-074).

requirements.statement: The add-address page is built from GOV.UK Frontend components (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link, width classes); the address search is the one component outside the toolbox, because GOV.UK Frontend has none.
requirements.why: The prototype's app-* field and heading classes are its own implementation, not a difference a trader sees.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (trace-e2e-p9-068).

requirements.statement: The add-address round trip (both saves and cancel) is proven end to end from every role picker, not only the consignor's.
requirements.why: Today only the consignor picker's round trip is proven, only on the compose stack, and no fit spec covers it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake specs drive only the consignor picker (repo-tests-p5-033, trace-e2e-p9-077) and only on compose (repo-tests-p5-032).

requirements.statement: A picked or added address is copied onto the notification, not linked: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record later leaves the draft's copy as it was, with no error, and the picker then neither preselects nor offers a deleted record.

requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-037, repo-tests-p5-042, repo-tests-p5-044, trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party and the contact address read back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address; the plants frontend's check-answers party cards change the same way in the same increment, with plants' own parties.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting; plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included, under the 'Roles and addresses' and 'Contact address for this consignment' cards (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018); plants' cards show telephone and email too.

requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-091, repo-tests-p5-053, trace-e2e-p8-031). Design Release 2.1 shows no such page in this area; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-122, repo-tests-p5-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' (blank or unlisted), 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length and email-format checks.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-tests-p5-063, repo-tests-p5-066, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051).

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-124, repo-tests-p5-068, trace-e2e-p8-047).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the role: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, the picker no longer preselects the source record, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-125, repo-frontend-p9-127, repo-tests-p5-061, repo-tests-p5-062, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save, Cancel and Back on the edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return parameter from a closed list (the addresses hub, the review page or the contact picker), falling back to the role's own return page and keeping change context; Cancel discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-129, repo-tests-p5-070, repo-tests-p5-071, trace-e2e-p8-057, trace-e2e-p8-058).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-130).

requirements.statement: The edit page has Welsh copy ('Golygu manylion cyfeiriad', 'Cadw’r newidiadau', 'Canslo'), marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Today's Welsh copy, which needs Welsh Language Standards sign-off before it ships to users.
requirements.deltaNote: Present today (repo-frontend-p9-132).

requirements.statement: The edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no axe violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p9-193, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name instead of a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-131, repo-tests-p5-045, trace-e2e-p8-013).

requirements.statement: The review keeps today's validation errors that Design Release 2.1 cannot show: an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>', 'Correct the contact address details for this consignment') linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the role's row, a stored answer that is no longer valid is named on its card, these come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-046, repo-tests-p5-050, trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-048, repo-tests-p5-049, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-051, repo-tests-p5-052, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view (status 'Submitted', no Change or Edit details links) nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-082, repo-tests-p5-085, trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084).

requirements.statement: Until address search is built, the consignee, importer and place of destination add-address pages open with the address and contact fields and the 'What else should this address be used for?' checkboxes shown at once, with no search box and no 'Enter address manually' control, so a trader can add any of those addresses by hand now.
requirements.why: Ruling 2026-10-09 blocks address search on the address lookup becoming a real feature but builds manual address entry now; a destination-side page that hid its fields behind a search that does not exist would leave no way to add the address.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page already shows every field at once for every role, with no search (trace-e2e-p9-058 to trace-e2e-p9-067); the uses checkboxes it gains are req-655.

requirements.statement: A trader adding an address from a germinal products notification's party picker crosses to the INS address book by the same handshake and the same INS add page, with the same address record and rules as live animals. The INS address book accepts the germinal products set as well as live animals, and saving or cancelling returns to the germinal set's own address-return page under /germinal-products/notifications/{notification id}, built on the server from a registered entry in the INS service's conventions, never to a live-animals notification.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a sibling set with its own journey, routes and cookies, and its notifications keep GBN-AG references; ruling 2026-10-09 puts the address-book return entry for the germinal set in the INS themes, proven in the ins Playwright project.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake carries journey-type 'gbn-ag' and the INS address book returns to the live-animals journey's /notifications/{id}/address-return route (trace-e2e-p9-014, trace-e2e-p9-070, repo-frontend-p9-139); no germinal set exists yet.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, address search results appear as the trader types, with the typed text in bold in each result.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type-ahead. Filtering as the trader types and match highlighting are JavaScript-only prototype mechanics, so they wait on design (questions 5 and 10) as well as on the lookup; the search works without them by its Search button (req-648).
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today (trace-e2e-p9-058).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design questions 5 (filtering as the trader types) and 10 (address search layout) (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), in the waiting-on-design theme; also blocked until the INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature, after which the address search area is re-distilled.

requirements.statement: When the INS add page is reached from the journey, it skips the address book's 'Choose an address type' step and opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the role implies, with that role already counted as the address's use.
requirements.why: The section the trader came from already says what kind of address it is (DR1 inc-053, c-106's outcome); asking again would be a wasted step.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type step at all: the journey lands straight on 'Add address details' (trace-e2e-p9-055, repo-tests-p5-027). The skip is new logic that must ship with the address book's type step (address-book-add-and-edit).

requirements.statement: A picker search that matches nothing ('No addresses match your search.') still leaves the 'Add a new address' link on the page, so a trader whose address is not in the book can add it instead of being stuck on 'Select a consignor from the list'.
requirements.why: DR1 found the empty search a dead end (inc-053); the add link now sits above the picker form whatever the search finds.
requirements.deltaNote: The picker renders the 'Add a new address' link above its form whenever the role has a handshake link, independent of the search results (repo-frontend-p9-133). The empty-state wording itself is the party picker area's.

requirements.statement: Each picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the INS address book, carrying the picker in a return parameter, so the trader can correct or delete the book record and come back to the picker they left; whether the in-place 'View details' disclosure stays is the party picker area's call, and if it stays it drops the name, address lines and country the row's columns already show.
requirements.why: DR1 asked for a way to correct a wrong saved address from the picker (inc-054), built together with the add route and leading to the same place; the INS frontend is the address book's only writer (c-106), so the record and its edit live there.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each picker row's 'View details' opens in place to show the record's fields, with no edit, delete or link out (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-036). Animals only: plants is not wired to the INS address book (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). Likely the same change as the party picker area's inc-090 'View' links; the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: Out of scope here: transporter list rows linking to the same saved-address record page.
requirements.why: Transporter management (adding, listing and searching transporters) waits on its requirements and is re-distilled once they are decided (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); DR1's record link on the transporter list goes with it.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the plants frontend takes no part in this area's add-address round trip, INS add page or notification copy edit pages.
requirements.why: Plants is not wired to the INS address book and has no handshake or party edit page today, and a row with no plants equivalent leaves plants alone (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). Plants takes only the review read-back (req-680).

conflicts.about: Where the journey's add-address page lives: inside the animals journey (Design Release 2.1) or on the INS frontend's address book reached by today's handshake.

positions.says: Each role has its own add-address page inside the journey at <section path>/add-address, which saves into the address book.
The prototype holds saved addresses in its own session and calls no address book or notification API, so it cannot show cross-service behaviour.
The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype.
DR1 left the destination for a person to choose: an add page in the animals frontend, or a link to the INS front door's add page with a way back.
The animals frontend's address-book service reads and never writes by design; the INS frontend is the address book's only writer.
Rhys blocked parity changes on the address pages on 2026-09-04 while the team's address work was live.
'Add a new address' goes to the INS frontend's /address-book/add page.
The animals journey no longer serves its own create-address page; the old route answers 404.
Outside Design Release 2.1, a section's add-address page redirects to the address book's add page with the section named in from.
The INS address book returns the trader to the journey's address-return page with the fulfilment id, address id and handshake token.
The prototype never decides architecture: the split into sets, journeys and services, URL paths or code structure.
c-106 is not architecture and is unchanged by the ruling.
INS-side germinal work, including the address-book return entry, stays in the INS themes and is proven in the ins Playwright project.
inc-053, the route to add an address from an address-selection page, is blocked by Rhys (2026-09-04) while the team's address work was live.
inc-054, correcting a wrong saved address from a picker, is blocked by Rhys (2026-09-04) for the same reason.
The missing add-address route is an accepted temporary gap: traders go to the address book by themselves.
inc-053 is frontend work because the address-book API already serves create; only where the add page lives is in dispute.

conflicts.outcome: Keep today's handshake and the INS frontend as the address book's only writer, because where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express (ruling 2026-10-07 claim 10), and ruling 2026-10-09 leaves this conflict unchanged (claim 126) and confirms the prototype never decides which service serves a page (claim 66). The page itself follows Design Release 2.1: 'Add a new address' still crosses to the INS frontend's /address-book/add, and when that page carries the journey handshake it shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page (caption, heading, status block, sections, fields, role split, other uses, buttons, messages, banner) and returns through the journey's address-return route to the page each button names ('Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing). In journey mode the INS add page skips 'Choose an address type' and opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the role implies, with the role's use ticked; outside a journey the address book's own add follows Design Release 2.1 in full. A germinal products notification uses the same handshake, with its own INS return entry built in the INS themes (ruling 2026-10-09 claim 61). The search parts of the page wait on the address lookup becoming a real feature; until then the consignee, importer and place of destination pages open on manual entry. Same on the compose stack and in CDP; in the animals frontend's stub mode (the fit suite), where no INS frontend runs, the pickers keep showing no add link. The animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only. The DR1 blocks on inc-053 and inc-054 (Rhys, 2026-09-04) and DR1's acceptance of the missing add route as a temporary gap are set aside: the team's address work has landed as today's handshake, and the later rulings put this area back in the programme. Each picker row's link to its record (req-party-address-add-and-edit-004) goes to the INS address book on the same reasoning; plants takes none of it, because plants is not wired to the INS address book (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). In journey mode the 'Choose an address type' step is skipped (req-party-address-add-and-edit-002).

conflicts.about: The manual-entry Country list: Design Release 2.1's 42 countries, regions and territories against today's 32 sovereign states.

positions.says: A parity finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list is deferred, not built, because MDM replaces the hard-coded list.
Countries, regions and territories are master reference data the service takes from MDM after the DR1 parity build.
Where DR1 already judged the same difference, its judgement is followed.
The Country select offers 42 entries, including the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies.
Today's Country select offers 32 sovereign states.
No reference list waits on MDM integration; every list is built now against reference-data as it is, and its content is what MDM serves.
Where a list's content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to block a row or to edit a list in code.
The block is taken off the requirements behind c-107, which rested on DR1's MDM judgement.
The INS Country select is reference-data's unfiltered /countries list.

conflicts.outcome: The later ruling (2026-10-09) ranks first and withdraws the MDM block this conflict once applied: req-644 is built now, unblocked, against reference-data as it is. The select offers what MDM serves; Design Release 2.1's 42-entry list is not built, because a list whose content differs from the design is MDM's to change, never edited in code. DR1's MDM judgement still stands for who owns list content (ruling 2026-10-09 claim 134), so document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-037 is not overruled; only its deferral rule (p1-038) is. The 'Select one' placeholder is not list content and is built (req-643).

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page checks only that required fields are filled (Design Release 2.1) or also keeps the address book's length and email-format checks (today).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, naming validation, overrides the prototype.
The address rules check email format, with 'Enter an email address in the correct format'.
The address rules cap postcode at 12 characters, with 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer'.
The add-address page only checks each required field is filled, with no format check on postcode, email or phone.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and names validation as a real constraint the prototype cannot express: the address book stores and checks these limits, so the add page keeps today's length and email-format checks and messages alongside Design Release 2.1's required-field messages. The prototype's required-only rule is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page follows the GOV.UK accessibility patterns the prototype leaves out: the 'Error: ' title prefix and 400 status on a refused submit, autocomplete hints on personal-data fields, and error summary links that reach a visible field.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
Today's address forms prefix the title with 'Error: ' when a submit is refused.
Today's address form fields carry autocomplete hints (address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, tel, email).
The prototype's refused submit keeps the plain title with no 'Error: ' prefix and answers 200.
No add-address input carries an autocomplete attribute.
On the search pages the error summary links point at fields that are hidden.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: how validation errors are reported, and what assistive technology needs from a form, are real constraints (GOV.UK error pattern, WCAG 2.2 AA under the public sector accessibility regulations) that a session-only prototype is not held to and does not express. The add page keeps the 'Error: ' prefix, the 400 status and autocomplete hints, and reveals the fields on the search pages so summary links reach them. The prototype's plain error title and missing autocomplete are set aside. trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-051 is not overruled: its six messages and their order still stand; only its hidden-field links are departed from.

conflicts.about: Address search's JavaScript-only behaviour in Design Release 2.1 (results as the trader types, the search-only layout that hides the fields, 'Enter address manually', custom announcements) against the 9 October afternoon ruling's graceful-degradation and toolbox rules.

positions.says: Results list as the trader types, with the typed text in bold.
The address fields and uses checkboxes stay hidden until a result is picked or manual entry is chosen.
Results appear in the browser as the trader types.
Every page works fully without JavaScript, and JavaScript may only enhance a page that already works.
The prototype's search mechanics are not copied; anything beyond the component's own options, such as custom announcements, waits on design.
Filtering as the trader types waits on design question 5; search on the Search button or Enter is built.
The fields hidden behind the search, 'Enter address manually' and the search-only layout that reveals the fields wait as one waiting-on-design increment (design question 10).
The rest of address search stays blocked on the address lookup, and the design increment is blocked on it too.
Design is asked whether address search can use the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first. When the address lookup lands, the version that works without JavaScript is built: a search form submitted by its 'Search' button (req-647), results on the returned page (req-648), and a pick that fills the fields (req-650). The JavaScript-only parts stay adopted but blocked on design as well as the lookup, in the waiting-on-design theme: results as the trader types with bold matches (req-party-address-add-and-edit-001), the custom result-count announcement (req-649), and the search-only layout with 'Enter address manually' and its errors (req-652, req-653, req-654). Until then every add-address page opens on manual entry with the fields shown (req-1830). Nothing is overruled: design may still keep or drop each behaviour.
